scope.title: Approval and recovery
scope.boundary: Real approval/executor/coordinator decisions and temporary Git evidence. Controlled providers expose observations, write histories and injected faults. These scenarios never authorize real publication or certify remote environment configuration.

initial_state: approval_fixture(): candidate a repeated 64, source b repeated 40 on refs/heads/main; repository xiongxianfei/rigorloop id 7; run 12 attempt 1, push, in_progress; artifact 13 with digest sha256:c repeated 64; protected release environment 9 and configured reviewer 2 approving. Each mutation owns a deep copy.

ReleaseExecutorTests.setUp creates real source/prepared commits, source bundle, two small target ZIPs, exact retained provider ZIP and digest, fake package bytes clearly excluded from package validity proof, matching FixtureApprovals/FixturePublisher, and a private bare Git evidence ref.

Approval facts plus protected main branch, settings evidence_ref=refs/heads/release-evidence and trusted_publisher=github:xiongxianfei/rigorloop:release.yml:release; event run_id=12, source=b repeated 40, source_ref=refs/heads/main, attempt=1.
The real-build fixture in candidate-identity.json, invoked through actual coordinator dispatch with FixtureHostedServices and local bare Git evidence.

cases.title: Only current provider approval for these retained bytes permits publication
cases.risk: Provider approval is reused for an unauthorized, changed or unretained candidate.

conditions: Use approval for policy checks and executor for retained-artifact/write observations. Start from mutually consistent provider, reviewer, workflow, candidate and digest facts.

Independently omit/reject approval, change a binding/provider identity or protection setting, supply a CI-only candidate, modify local bytes, or substitute a new seal/retained ZIP. Pair an unknown binding field with a candidate mismatch.

when: Validate policy in a fresh process, including absent/malformed unrelated package metadata; execute the actual publication boundary with rejected or substituted inputs.
then: Valid provider approval identifies the exact candidate/reviewer independently of package generation.
Missing, stale, unknown or mismatched authority and unsafe/corrupt retained ZIP content reject. Unknown fields reject before identity consistency.
Rejected authority or changed local/retained bytes produces no public write; a new local seal cannot reuse the old provider artifact approval.

gaps: Unknown binding fields reject before identity consistency: Existing test supplies only the extra field; add the simultaneous candidate mismatch to establish precedence explicitly.

cases.title: Durable evidence is established before publication and preserves neighbors
cases.risk: Concurrent reporting loses another release observation.

conditions: Use executor with a private bare Git evidence ref, a neighboring release and independent expected head. Inject a ref conflict, source-ref collision or initial persistence failure.

when: Persist the initial attempt and execute publication when persistence succeeds; repeat with each storage fault.
then: Compare-and-swap writes preserve neighboring releases and cannot target the source branch.
Failed initial durable recording prevents every publication write.

cases.title: Concurrent or duplicate evidence writes cannot take over an active attempt
cases.risk: Two attempts race after observing an absent immutable boundary.

conditions: Use executor with an already active durable attempt; separately mirror identical and conflicting evidence bytes.

when: Start a competing execution and exercise the actual evidence mirror.
then: The active attempt excludes a competing writer. Identical mirrored bytes are reusable; conflicting bytes stop without overwrite.

cases.title: Lost reporting preserves publication observations and requires safe recovery
cases.risk: Lost reporting erases the public-write fact and causes another publication.

conditions: Use executor. Fail persistence after a public write; separately resume without its retained observation artifact.

when: Execute, inspect preserved observations/failure status and retry unchanged inputs through actual recovery.
then: A public write followed by reporting failure remains incomplete closeout; observations are retained.
Retry never republishes the completed immutable operation. Missing recovery observations require intervention rather than inferred success.

cases.title: One approval completes the actual routine path and duplicate delivery is safe
cases.risk: Individually correct helpers are wired into a coordinator that bypasses approval, rebuilds bytes, hides failures or publishes twice.

conditions: Use hosted-composition with actual preparation/build/coordinator dispatch, one fixture approval, retained artifacts and local provider/evidence substitutes.

when: Drive prepare, qualify, approve, execute, observe and report through the real coordinator.
Repeat delivery; drive a controlled smoke/reporting failure through real dispatch and resume from retained state; compare unchanged already-published source with changed source lacking a new version.
then: The protected executor publishes the retained tarball/archives through the selected OIDC path and records actual outcomes after exactly one candidate approval.
Workflow composition retains one protected executor and required local/CI gate parity.
Duplicates and unchanged published source perform no second immutable write; actual dispatch preserves failures during recovery. Changed source needs new version intent.

cases.title: Missing setup or runtime credentials stops before publication authority
cases.risk: The coordinator requests approval for an unprotected or misconfigured source.

conditions: Use setup with independently defined reviewer/environment/branch protection, evidence ref and trusted publisher; remove one prerequisite at a time.

when: Inspect setup and enter the actual coordinator with each missing/unprotected fact or missing required credential.
then: Report inspected configuration and distinguish it from runtime authorization.
Missing protection or credentials prevents the approval/publication path with the prerequisite named; configuration inspection itself grants no permission.

cases.title: Unknown or uncertain publication is resolved by bounded observation before retry
cases.risk: Unavailable or delayed public state causes an unbounded wait, false success or duplicate immutable publication.

conditions: Use executor with known prior boundaries. Independently make initial npm state unavailable, lose a write response, time out a subprocess, or hide the post-write identity until the last observation or beyond the limit.
For exhaustion count observations after the write: tag/GitHub allow six with waits 0..4; npm allows 121 with waits 0..119. Use controlled waits without sleeping.

when: Execute and inspect write/observation history and durable attempt state.
Expose the matching committed identity after uncertainty, then retry unchanged inputs. Also supply an unknown stored state or execution boundary.
then: Unobservable initial state grants no write permission. A lost response is resolved from actual public state, never by blind republish.
Matching identity on the last admitted observation permits progress. Exhaustion records uncertain-publication and its boundary, clears active execution, performs no extra wait or later write.
Retry observes the committed identity and resumes without repeating its immutable write. Unknown execution state/boundary rejects.

gaps: Visibility exhaustion stops at its exact boundary and recovers by observation: Existing tests cover npm success on observation 121 and unknown tag outcome; add explicit exhaustion counts and recovery at every boundary.

cases.title: Partial GitHub assets resume only the missing operation
cases.risk: Incomplete asset publication restarts every boundary.

conditions: Prepublish matching tag/GitHub data, remove one observed GitHub asset and clear the call history while retaining public state.

then: Write history is exactly [github, npm]; the matching tag is not written again.

cases.title: Failed smoke or changed public identity leaves publication failed until corrected
cases.risk: Successful initial writes conceal failed public installation or identity drift during closeout.

conditions: Use executor after matching publication. Independently fail smoke, mismatch installed tree, or change npm dist-tag from candidate 0.5.1 to 0.5.0 during smoke before final observation.

when: Finish closeout, inspect failure evidence, then repair only the failed observation and retry the unchanged candidate.
then: Persist failed-after-publication and retain published identity and failure history; no completed status is recorded while smoke, installed bytes or final public identity disagree.
Retry repairs closeout by observation; publication writes are not repeated.

gaps: Public identity changes during smoke prevent completed closeout: Add an explicit change during closeout; initial conflict and installed-tree mismatch tests cover different boundaries.

cases.title: Conflicting public identity is never overwritten
cases.risk: An immutable name conflict is treated as missing publication.

conditions: Prepopulate the public tag observation with commit=f repeated 40, differing from prepared_commit.

then: Raise ExecutionError and leave publication write history empty.

cases.title: Actual CLI diagnostics suppress private failure details
cases.risk: Exception formatting leaks local secrets or converts an operational failure to success.

conditions: For read-evidence inject PermissionError naming /private/worker/user/release-secret. For check-ci inject OSError, FileNotFoundError(errno=2), CandidateError with a private log path, KeyError, TypeError and AttributeError.

when: Invoke the real dispatcher with controlled services; capture stderr and any GitHub summary file.
then: Every variant exits 1 and excludes /private/worker from user-visible output.
check-ci reports CI release preparation stopped:; the errno=2 variant preserves OS error 2 without its path.

cases.title: Authority revoked between boundaries prevents subsequent writes
cases.risk: Only the initial approval check protects a multi-boundary publication.

conditions: Allow tag publication and matching observation, then return rejected approval facts on the next approvals.fetch call while the sealed candidate remains unchanged.

then: Execution raises ExecutionError before GitHub/npm writes; the tag observation remains recorded and total write history is [tag].

gaps: Authority revoked between boundaries prevents subsequent writes: Add a provider-fact change between actual boundaries; initial rejection tests do not establish repeated safeguards.
